newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ivory Coast forecasts 1.15 mln tonne cocoa crop.
newsitem.headline: Ivory Coast forecasts 1.15 mln tonne cocoa crop.

text.p: Ivory Coast's 1996/97 (October-September) cocoa crop is set to reach 1.15 million tonnes, slightly below last year's record, while the coffee crop almost doubled to 325,000 tonnes, the government daily newspaper said.

"Ivory Coast's coffee production has almost doubled compared to the 1995/96 campaign," according to a crop summary published in Fraternite Matin on Monday which put the 1996/97 crop at around 325,000 tonnes, against about 170,000 tonnes in 1995/96.
Official forecasts had ranged between 250,000 and 270,000 tonnes, it added.
"(Cocoa) production should reach 1.15 million tonnes, or a bit less than the preceding exceptional crop (1.2 million)," the summary said.
Ivory Coast rarely publishes crop data until well after seasons have been closed.
Port sources put the total amount of cocoa taken to ports by July 13 in a 1.06-1.7 million tonnes range, with coffee at 308,000 tonnes by July 18.
Ivory Coast originally forecast a cocoa crop of up to 950,000 tonnes, with coffee seen at 230,000 tonnes.
Sources said last year's coffee crop totalled 180,000 tonnes.
Exporters and buyers expecting a farmgate price rise in 1997/98 have said some of this year's crops is likely be retained for sale from October onwards.
Agriculture Minister Lambert Kouassi Konan said in a recent interview with a Paris-based magazine that a coffee price rise was likely.

Last year's coffee season was opened late in mid-November, rather than early October, in an attempt to set the farm price closer to world levels expected for the main marketing period from February onwards.
